package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Spring Framework allow attackers to manipulate internal ClassLoader attributes via HTTP POST parameter binding, enabling remote code execution (RCE) by writing arbitrary files (such as web shells) to accessible locations on the server. This is a critical security vulnerability (CVE-2022-22965) that can be exploited remotely without authentication.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request to a Spring endpoint accepting POJOs)
execution_context.file_location: Any Spring Web Controller endpoint that binds POST parameters to objects

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends specially crafted POST parameters to a vulnerable Spring endpoint, reconfiguring Tomcat's logging to write a file with a .jsp extension containing attacker-controlled code to a web-accessible directory. This results in arbitrary file write and remote code execution when the file is accessed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows external users to overwrite server configuration and write executable files to the web root, which is a classic RCE pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal POST parameter binding should not allow access to internal server configuration or file system manipulation. Here, user input is mapped directly to sensitive server internals.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of POST parameter binding is for mapping user input to business objects, not for server reconfiguration.
key_indicators: Manipulation of Tomcat pipeline attributes via HTTP request
Writing files with .jsp extension to web-accessible directories

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies a POST endpoint in a Spring application that binds request parameters to POJOs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to send crafted POST requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a POST request with parameters that reconfigure Tomcat's logging to write a .jsp file containing malicious code to a web-accessible directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary file write of a web shell

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the written .jsp file via HTTP, triggering execution of the malicious code on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution (RCE) on the server

behavioral_signatures: POST requests with parameters prefixed by class.module.classLoader.*
Unexpected changes to Tomcat logging configuration at runtime
Creation of new .jsp files in web-accessible directories
file_indicators: webapps/ROOT/*.jsp files created or modified unexpectedly
Log files with .jsp extension containing web shell code
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to Spring endpoints with suspicious parameter names
Subsequent HTTP GET requests to newly created .jsp files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing parameters such as class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.*. Alert on creation of new .jsp files in web-accessible directories, especially if the file content matches common web shell patterns. Review Tomcat configuration changes at runtime and correlate with suspicious HTTP activity.
